title: Data Scientist
tagline: Turn data into decisions with statistics, experiments and models.
about: Data scientists answer questions with data: why did sign-ups drop, which feature works, what will demand look like next quarter? You'll clean data, explore it, run experiments, build models and, most importantly, communicate findings that change decisions.
Strong statistics and clear communication matter as much as coding.
day: Partner with product and business teams

phases.title: Programming foundations
phases.goal: Write small programs confidently and use the tools every developer uses daily.

nodes.d: Pick Python and get fluent with the basics before anything else. Fluency in one language transfers to every other.
links: CS50x: Harvard's intro to computer science

nodes.d: Developers live in the command line: navigating files, running programs and chaining tools together.
links: The Missing Semester of Your CS Education (MIT)
OverTheWire: Bandit (learn the shell by playing)

nodes.d: Version control is non-negotiable: every job uses it. Commit early, branch for experiments, open pull requests.
Break problems down, read errors calmly, use a debugger and print statements deliberately.
links: Exercism: practice in 70+ languages with mentoring

phases.title: Data wrangling
phases.goal: Load, clean, reshape and query data fluently.

nodes.d: Most company data lives in SQL warehouses. Window functions are your best friend.
DataFrames: filtering, grouping, joining and reshaping.
Missing values, duplicates, outliers and messy types: 80% of the job.
Charts that reveal patterns and tell honest stories.

project.d: Take a public dataset, clean it, find three non-obvious insights, and publish a notebook with clear charts and a one-page summary.

nodes.d: Distributions, conditional probability and Bayes' rule.
links: Seeing Theory: visual probability and statistics

nodes.d: Estimates, confidence intervals and hypothesis tests, and what p-values do and don't mean.
links: An Introduction to Statistical Learning (free book)

nodes.d: Design experiments that give trustworthy answers.
links: Evan Miller: A/B testing tools and articles

nodes.d: Model relationships and interpret coefficients carefully.
links: An Introduction to Statistical Learning (free book)

nodes.d: Correlation isn't causation: methods for causal questions with observational data.

phases.title: Machine learning
phases.goal: Predict and segment with models you can explain.

nodes.d: Regression and classification with scikit-learn.
links: An Introduction to Statistical Learning (free book)

nodes.d: Clustering and segmentation.
Explain predictions to stakeholders.
Forecast demand and metrics.
When neural networks beat classical methods.
links: fast.ai: Practical Deep Learning for Coders

project.t: Predictive model with a business story
project.d: Build a churn or demand model, explain its drivers with SHAP, and present a recommendation with expected impact.

nodes.d: Lead with the answer, show the evidence, recommend an action.
Define metrics well and monitor them.
Reproducible pipelines and scheduled reports.
Fairness, consent and handling personal data.

interview: SQL live coding with window functions.
Statistics: design and interpret an A/B test; explain a p-value.
Product case: a metric dropped 10%, how do you investigate?
ML fundamentals and a take-home analysis.
